match_note: The first-round reports cite content that appears in arXiv v1. Examples: Fig. 2E P-up/P-down patterns; Fig. S2 integrated over 140x140 nm2; 60 nm thickness; Fig. 4D nucleation schematic against the 111 K map; Figs. S4/S5; the 69-91 K periodic ordering with lambda ~25 nm; Ref. [21] Eq. (1); and the page-2 claim that 'quantum paraelectrics are governed by nanoscale polar domains'. The typos R2 lists ('parelectric' in the abstract, 'strain-incduced', 'paraelectricty', 'paraelecric' on p.6) are all present in v1. The only visible difference is the title ('Imaging of Nanoscale Polar Textures...' vs v1 'Nanoscale Polar Landscapes...'), which is likely the final title. Round structure: Version 0 has R1, R2 and R3. In Version 1, R1's remarks are blank in the file, but the rebuttal quotes a brief informal comment from R1; R2 and R3 also commented. In Version 2 only R2 commented, supporting acceptance.

concerns.quote: The manuscript and its supplementary information mostly show highly processed “data”. I find this highly concerning. There is no raw data
concerns.summary: Only processed polar maps are shown, with no raw 4D-STEM data to show that the underlying patterns contain polarity information.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: In Fig. 2E, visually it is impossible to tell a difference between P up and P down from these patterns... the difference in the line scan... is simply an artifact.
concerns.summary: The experimental P-up and P-down Kikuchi patterns look identical despite extreme intensity scaling, unlike the PbTiO3 work, so the line-scan difference may be an artifact.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it is integrated over 140 nm x 140 nm, much larger than the claimed size of the nanodomains. It is therefore not clear how spatially resolved maps can be obtained
concerns.summary: The Fig. S2 pattern is blurry and averaged over the whole field of view, so it is unclear how nanoscale maps follow from such data.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: The sample thickness is given as 60 nm. This is larger than the size of the (claimed) polar nanodomains... which will wash out any information about their polarization directions.
concerns.summary: Domains with different polarization stacked through the 60 nm thickness should average out the signal along the beam direction.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The manuscript lacks crucial information about important experimental parameters and limitations, such as sample drift, how it changes with temperature, noise, estimations of errors, etc.
concerns.summary: Drift, noise, error estimates and raw-data quality as a function of temperature are not reported.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the authors claim that the domains break up at lower temperatures. This could simply be an artifact from sample drift increasing at lower temperatures
concerns.summary: The apparent low-temperature fragmentation could be caused by increased sample drift washing out the polarization signal.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: not the first use of the analysis methodology, the specific STEM holder, or of liquid-He microscopy in general
concerns.summary: The technique, holder and liquid-He STEM are not new.
concerns.response: not addressed

concerns.quote: make no attempt to reconcile other proposed structures. For example, sheet and anti-phase boundary-like structures from diffuse scattering have been proposed..., as well as locally polar mobile twin boundaries
concerns.summary: The results are not reconciled with competing models such as antiphase-boundary sheets or polar mobile AFD twin walls.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: The magnitudes (saturation of the colored maps) as presented suggest that even above the bulk AFD transition, there is large non-zero polarization when the expected structure should be paraelectric.
concerns.summary: The saturated maps imply substantial polarization above T_AFD, which is unexplained and could reflect altered transition temperatures.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: I do not see how the model of polar domain nucleation in Fig. 4D is supported by the map at 111 K in Fig. 4A.
concerns.summary: The 111 K map already looks largely polar, so it does not support the nucleation picture in Fig. 4D.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: I therefore ask the authors to provide direct experimental evidence of the cubic-to-tetragonal symmetry change associated with the AFD transition.
concerns.summary: The AFD transition is inferred only indirectly from polar maps; direct evidence of AFD onset, intermediate temperatures between 111 K and RT, or rotation quantification is needed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: my main objection is whether the low-T fragmentation is a lamella effect... the thin geometry provides unconstrained free surfaces.
concerns.summary: Free surfaces, relaxed boundary conditions or size effects in the thin lamella, which can suppress AFD or shift transitions, may cause the behaviour rather than intrinsic bulk physics.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Did the authors verify the initial composition or see any changing oxygen off-stoichiometry?
concerns.summary: Oxygen vacancies or off-stoichiometry could alter or induce the polar disorder, and composition was not checked.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it is necessary to have simulations of varying polar displacements and mis-tilt, and at what point this method is no longer reliable especially for a centrosymmetric paraelectric such as STO
concerns.summary: Simulations are needed to establish how sample mis-tilt affects the Kikuchi asymmetry and where the method breaks down for weakly polar STO.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: It should also be possible to map mis-tilts from the experimental data as well.
concerns.summary: Local mis-tilt should be mapped experimentally to check whether it mimics polar textures.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Did the authors see any dose or other electron beam dependence of the polar structures (which can be due to local charging or heating)?
concerns.summary: Beam-induced charging or heating could modify the polar structures.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: are the maps (reflecting the static domain structure) identical across additional acquisitions for the same region and temperature
concerns.summary: Repeat acquisitions are needed to check whether the textures are static or time-varying.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Additional information on sample/lamella mounting geometry is necessary, as thermal mismatch can affect the boundary conditions.
concerns.summary: The lamella mounting is not described, so thermal-mismatch strain cannot be assessed.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: The Kikuchi bands are not orthogonal as compared to the simulated structure (Fig 2C vs 2E). Is this an artifact of the projection lenses
concerns.summary: The non-orthogonal Kikuchi bands could be a lens distortion or a temperature-dependent structural change.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Are COM shift magnitudes normalized across temperatures, or all to the room temperature paraelectric data (comparing the main text figures with Fig. S4)? This is unclear.
concerns.summary: It is unclear how COM magnitudes are normalized between temperatures.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Can the COM shift magnitudes be translated to a real-space polar displacement value?
concerns.summary: COM shifts are not calibrated to actual ionic displacements.
concerns.response: partly

concerns.quote: there is an on average drop in the background with decreasing temperature (Fig. 4B, Fig. S5)... Could this relate to changes associated with the AFD transition?
concerns.summary: The cause of the temperature-dependent background in the FFT radial profiles is unexplained.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The size of polar domains appears inhomogeneous from left to right (gradient) in Fig. 3C and Fig 4 at lower temperatures. Is there any significance to this?
concerns.summary: A lateral gradient in domain size at low temperature is unexplained and could be an artifact.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The 2D correlation plots and polar maps show directional dependence of the periodic structures. Can the authors comment on the origin of this texture?
concerns.summary: The origin of the anisotropic, directional periodic texture is not discussed.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: Several typos: a. ‘parelectric’ in abstract b. ‘strain-incduced’ in introduction paragraph 1
concerns.summary: There are several typographical errors.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: the periodic ordering of polar nanodomains is reported between 69K and 91K... bulk neutron studies typically observe the analogous mesoscopic fluctuations only at much lower temperatures (≈ 20K)
concerns.summary: The ordering temperature conflicts with bulk neutron data, raising whether the upward shift is a lamella size effect or an artifact.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: the ordering length, λ ≈ 25nm is also slightly different from previously reported values (≈ 16nm).
concerns.summary: The 25 nm periodicity differs from the ~16 nm length inferred from neutron scattering.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: The experimentally derived autocorrelation function C(r) at 69K bear a qualitative resemblance to the theoretical predictions in Ref. [21]... whether an explicit comparison is warranted.
concerns.summary: The authors should discuss, and possibly compare explicitly, the resemblance of C(r) to melted incommensurate (lamellar) order theory.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

concerns.quote: The term "quantum paraelectrics" is an umbrella term covering a broad class of materials... I therefore ask the authors to rephrase these statements to refer specifically to STO
concerns.summary: The claims overgeneralize from lamella STO to all quantum paraelectrics.
concerns.response: addressed by argument or rewording

later_concerns.quote: decreasing intensity of the beam does not mean it gets "lost" - rather, it broadens and scatters from surrounding regions.
later_concerns.summary: R1 criticized one rebuttal statement describing beam intensity as 'lost' with depth; the referee's text appears only as quoted in the authors' rebuttal.

later_concerns.quote: I would highly encourage the authors to make available the analysis code and all presented experimental datasets at a minimum.
later_concerns.summary: The code and datasets should be released.

later_concerns.quote: A more direct comparison of the COM shifts and autocorrelations between the polar structure and mis-tilt (Fig R12) may be beneficial
later_concerns.summary: COM shift and autocorrelation maps should be compared directly against mis-tilt maps.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: I would also encourage inclusion of time dependence (R14) and the sample mounting geometry (R15) in the supplemental materials.
later_concerns.summary: The rebuttal figures on repeatability and mounting should be added to the SI.

later_concerns.quote: is averaging of several scan pixels necessary for arriving at similar results using the additional direct method (scaled k)?
later_concerns.summary: Does the k-scaled antisymmetry method need spatial averaging, or does it work on single pixels?
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the COM uncertainty estimation in Figure R7, which uses 2x2 pixel averaging. Are the results presented in the main text and supplement using consistent averaging, or are they pixel by pixel?
later_concerns.summary: The averaging used for the uncertainty estimate is inconsistent with that used for the maps.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: is the new analysis approach with the scaled k used to update the main text results, or does it only serve as a spot check of the old method?
later_concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the main results use the new k-scaled method or only the original COM method.

later_concerns.quote: what is the effect of shifting the kx and ky masks on the detector? Is there tolerance of the measured polar shift to mask offsets/error of a few detector pixels?
later_concerns.summary: The sensitivity of the COM shift to mask offsets and beam-centering errors is untested.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: I am not an expert in cryogenic 4D-STEM... I cannot independently judge whether these additions fully resolve that experimental concern. I therefore defer to the referees with the appropriate experimental expertise
later_concerns.summary: R3 now supports publication but defers judgment on whether the raw-data additions resolve R1's validation concern.

first_round.quote: I do not recommend that this manuscript be published in Nature or any other journal for the following reasons
However, I have several remaining concerns regarding the analyses and interpretation
I am not convinced the findings fully support the claims made. Therefore, I cannot recommend the manuscript for publication in its present form.

recommendations.note: Ratings use the first round (Version 0); the file shows no transfer from another journal. R1 is marked explicit because it plainly refuses publication in any journal, though it never uses the word 'reject'. R2 gives no verdict; 'major revision' is inferred from its requests for new simulations (mis-tilt, polar displacement), AFD-onset quantification, oxygen-stoichiometry checks, and beam-dose and strain information. R3 is inferred as 'major revision' rather than 'reject' because 'in its present form' and its request for direct evidence of the AFD symmetry change point to resubmission after new data. R1's later-round remarks are blank in the file but are summarised in the authors' second rebuttal.
recommendations.label: contested
